title: Speech and Voice Changes in Parkinson's
content: Parkinson's disease can affect speech and voice. Some people may develop a softer or quieter voice, reduced vocal expression, changes in pitch, unclear articulation, rapid speech or difficulty being heard and understood. Speech changes can develop gradually and vary between individuals. Speech-language pathologists can assess communication difficulties and provide therapies or strategies to support clearer and more effective communication. Voice or speech changes alone do not confirm Parkinson's disease because they can have many other causes.
